resources.string: MilkDrop uses a customized projectM engine to run MilkDrop presets. Its patches improve BeatDrop compatibility for waveforms, FFT shader functions, accurate beat detection, textures, preset variables and pixel alignment, and add date/time and touch input.

FPS shows how many frames the visualizer renders each second; it may differ from the frame-rate setting and the TV’s playback rate. The version and commit identify the source bundled with this app, rather than the latest online release. Engine updates arrive with app updates.
Connecting to %1$s…\nPress Back to stop receiving.
The display is still connected. Disconnect it in your phone’s connection settings to stop sharing.
Optional: allow Nearby devices or Location access to identify your connected TV or projector. Casting still works without it.
Your visuals are playing on your TV or projector. Google Cast video may be several seconds behind. Control presets and settings from this device.
Open your phone’s connection settings to find Miracast or Smart View displays. After connecting, return to MilkDrop. Available options depend on your phone and TV.
Wireless display settings aren’t available on this device.
Your visuals are playing on your TV or projector. Control presets and settings from this device. Tap here to show or hide the controls.
Couldn’t cast to this device. Check the connection and try again.

This device reports %1$s, but MilkDrop needs a working OpenGL ES 3.0 graphics context. OpenGL ES 2.0 devices cannot run this projectM renderer. Audio and storage permissions cannot enable the missing graphics features. You can connect a compatible Android TV device to a projector by HDMI.
Instant switches presets without a fade. Random chooses a new fade duration between 0 and 5 seconds for each preset change.
Max removes the app’s FPS limit. Actual speed depends on your display and device. Google Cast targets up to 60 FPS, depending on encoder and receiver support.
Controls warp detail independently of Quality. Higher values improve curved and detailed warps but use more CPU time.

Auto respects your frame-rate setting and adjusts resolution around 50–60 FPS. For limits below 50 FPS, the range scales down to match. Currently using %1$s (%2$d%% of display width and height). Mesh size stays unchanged.
%1$s renders at %2$d%% of display resolution. Mesh size stays unchanged.
Uses Internal audio when available and the microphone during silence. Switches back when playback resumes.
Auto is listening to audio playing on your device.
Auto is using the microphone while Internal audio is silent or unavailable.
Auto is waiting for audio input. Check microphone access or start playback.
Listens through your microphone, picking up music from speakers and sounds around you.
Captures playback without a capture popup by default. Enable Stereo internal audio below for separate left and right channels. Some apps block capture.
Optional for Internal and Auto on Android 10 or newer. Android asks for capture consent each session. Uses mono if unavailable or declined. Off by default; microphone stereo is independent.
Playback audio is driving your visuals.
Internal audio is unavailable on this device, so the mic is on.
The microphone is unavailable. Check that another app isn\'t using it, then try again.
Allow microphone access in Android settings to enable audio input.
Adjusts the audio level used by the visuals without changing playback volume.
No presets found. Try different search words.
No favourite presets found. Try different search words or turn off the favourites filter.
Unable to start visuals on this device.
No presets found. Add .milk files to MilkDropApp/presets, then reopen the app.
Allow All files access so the app can read MilkDropApp/presets.
Unable to create the presets or textures folder. Check storage access and available space.
